sources.entry: Roughcut - Turns a folder of talking-head footage into a rough cut in Final Cut Pro, with on-device Whisper transcription and cuts chosen by a local or cloud AI model. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/Bouliw/fcpxml-roughcut) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: A macOS command-line and app toolkit that turns a folder of talking-head footage into a frame-accurate rough cut in Final Cut Pro, using on-device Whisper transcription and AI-chosen cuts.
summary.what_it_does: The tool transcribes each clip word by word with whisper.cpp on the Mac, then either a person or an AI model (Claude Code, a local OpenAI-compatible server, or an API key) writes the chosen cuts into an edl.json file. Scripts convert that file into a frame-accurate FCPXML timeline validated against Final Cut Pro's DTD, SRT subtitles, and a loudness-normalized 1080p preview. Optional steps cover dialogue level matching, punch-in zooms on jump cuts, J and L split edits, B-roll and music placement, and vertical Shorts with face-following framing and animated captions. A separate Roughcut macOS app wraps the scripts with a drop-folder interface, and a Finder Quick Action runs the whole pipeline on a selected folder. The README describes footage analysis (sharpness, shake, exposure, faces via Apple Vision) that proposes rejected ranges and B-roll candidates.
use_cases: rough-cut a talking-head video before finishing it in Final Cut Pro
remove pauses, ums and false starts from a recorded take
generate YouTube subtitles and chapters from footage
make vertical Shorts with animated captions from long videos
transcribe interview or vlog footage locally without uploading
batch-edit a folder of camera clips from the Finder
stack: Python 3 (standard library for core scripts; numpy and pyobjc-framework-Vision optional for analysis)
librosa or fcp-mcp-server via uvx (music tempo, optional)
Anthropic SDK / Claude Code, LM Studio or Ollama, OpenAI-compatible API (brain options)
notable: Frame-accurate rational time math, handling 29.97 and 59.94 fps, with camera timecode preserved
Every generated FCPXML is validated against the DTD inside the installed Final Cut Pro before use
Transcription runs locally with whisper.cpp; the README states no footage is uploaded
Optional macOS app (Roughcut) with a drop-folder interface and a Finder Quick Action built on the same engine
Experimental B-roll finder skill for Claude Code is included but off by default
caveats: Requires macOS with Apple silicon, Final Cut Pro, and about 3 GB of free space for the app's tools and model; the README states the app was tested on macOS 26.5 only and not yet on macOS 14 or 15.
The Roughcut app is ad hoc signed and not notarized yet, so macOS requires an Open Anyway step on first launch unless a Developer ID is used to build it.
The Claude brain sends transcripts to Anthropic; only the local brain keeps everything on the Mac. The B-roll finder module is described as experimental and not yet tried on a real edit.
summary.license: MIT (for the app and scripts, per the README; bundled tools keep their own licenses)
